title: Deployment Runway Index & Network Readiness Playbook for Private Requests
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Problem: We receive high-variance private/VPC/on-prem deployment requests that require manual, ad-hoc triage for networking and upgrade constraints (air-gapped, strict firewall, Windows-based networks). This slows time-to-yes, creates repeated engineering gatekeeping, and causes inconsistent communication to customers.

Goal: Create a repeatable, lightweight 'Deployment Runway Index' (DRI) and an accompanying Network Readiness Playbook that: 1) provides a deterministic numeric runway score for each intake request, 2) surfaces exact remediation steps and estimated engineering runway (days), and 3) embeds a human-review escalation flow for high-risk items. The DRI will be used to prioritize backlog, select SLA tier, and gate Private deployment offers.

Scope: Non-bug product requests related to Private/VPC/on-prem deployments (networking, upgrade sequence, air-gap constraints, OS/platform compatibility). Excludes large custom engineering projects that require >60 engineering days (these become scoped as enterprise engagements).

Why different: Rather than a binary eligible/not-eligible gate, the DRI produces a graded runway (0-100) combining network technical readiness, upgrade complexity, security controls, and dependency risk. This supports graduated offers (self-serve, assisted onboarding, enterprise track).
acceptance_criteria: A DRI calculation spec (weights and signals) documented and reviewed by Eng & Security
A one-page Network Readiness Playbook artifact with checklist items, probe commands, and remediation templates
Intake form updated to capture all DRI signals and automatically compute a baseline score
Two pilot accounts (internal + one low-risk partner) processed end-to-end using DRI with time-to-decision measured
Routing rules defined: score buckets -> (self-serve / SE-assisted / enterprise sales), and integrated into the intake dashboard

2025-01-16 - Liam C.: Proposed initial weight matrix: network 40%, upgrade 30%, security controls 20%, dependencies 10%. Suggested adding an automated probe to validate firewall egress and DNS resolution as a required signal.

2025-01-20 - Sophie L. (Security): Security review required for any score >80 that still requests private self-serve. Recommend adding minimum KMS/HSM policy checks and audit log availability as binary gates.

2025-01-24 - Marina A.: Created intake form prototype and mapped fields to DRI signals. Noted ambiguity around 'upgrade runway' estimation; will surface as engineering-days estimate with confidence buckets (Low/Medium/High).

2025-01-28 - Liam C.: ENG spike approved (ENG-12014) to build a lightweight network probe CLI and a server-side scheduler to run probes during intake. ETA for spike: 2 weeks. Asked PM to prioritize top 10 onboarding questions to minimize probe surface area.

2025-02-02 - Marina A.: Alignment session notes: 1) Use score buckets [0-30,31-60,61-85,86-100] mapped to routing rules, 2) Playbook to include remediation templates and comms copy for customer-facing SEs, 3) Pilot goal: reduce manual triage time by 50%.

decisions: DRI will be numeric 0-100 to allow fine-grained prioritization and machine-routable buckets
Automated network probe required for minimum score (probe results adjust score, not a hard block)
High-security requirements (KMS/HSM missing, audit logs disabled) will downgrade self-serve eligibility regardless of DRI
Enterprise engagements (estimated engineering runway >60 days) will bypass DRI and move to Sales-led scoping
